user.title: Home Thermal Lab
user.description:
Set the house once: the outdoor temperature sensor, how the house is turned and its roofs.

{map}

Then, on the integration's page, add the sensors in this order:
1. Heating-call statistics: one per zone (thermostat only).
2. Furnace energy: one for the blower (pick your whole-house power sensor and it learns the blower power) and one for the gas (type the furnace input in BTU/h).
3. Shadow zone (with sun): one per zone. Leave the model blank and it learns it from the last 14 days.
4. Contribution chart: one per zone, once you have its fitted terms.

data.ground_coldest_day: Ground temperature: coldest day of the year
data.infiltration_ach: Loads: air leakage (air changes per hour)

data_description.outdoor_entity: Used by the shadow zone and the contribution chart.
data_description.rotation: Degrees the house is turned clockwise from true north: the measured value is filled in. Set once here, for every room.
data_description.shade_below: Treat the south-east to south-west sun as blocked below this elevation (trees, neighbours). A room can set its own.
data_description.roofs: Each roof of the house with windows or skylights: face and pitch, with a name you choose, for example: Front=S 30, Back=W 4:12, Garage=W 8:12. The pitch is in degrees or as rise:run. Rooms refer to a roof by its name, so you can change a pitch later and every room keeps its link. Without a name a roof is called after its face (West, West 2); the form then shows the names. If you rename a roof (keep its face), the rooms that use it follow the new name. Deleting a roof unlinks them.
data_description.preview: Tick and press Submit to redraw the map with the rotation typed above. Nothing is saved until you submit with this unticked.
data_description.ground_mean: For below-ground rooms without a ground sensor. Leave empty for the defaults (5.7, 5.6 and 95), measured at 1.8 m in Regina (hypothesis 03).
data_description.ground_swing: Half the gap between the warmest and coldest ground. About 0.4 of the air's swing at basement depth.
data_description.ground_coldest_day: Day of the year (1 to 365) the ground is coldest: roughly 70 days after the coldest air at basement depth.
data_description.infiltration_ach: Natural air changes per hour for the Manual J. Leave empty for 0.35, a fairly tight house; an older house is often 0.5 to 0.7. From a blower-door test, roughly ACH50 divided by 20.
data_description.wall_r: The effective R-value of the outside walls, studs included (R-20 batts in 2x6 framing are about R-15 overall). Leave empty for R-20. A wall part in House Structure with its own R-value keeps it.
data_description.roof_r: The effective R-value of the ceilings under the roof. Leave empty for R-35. A roof part with its own R-value keeps it.
data_description.basement_floor_r: The basement slab and the soil under it, as one effective R-value against the design ground temperature. Leave empty for R-11, an uninsulated slab.

user.title: Heating-call statistics
user.description: Length, rise, lag, overshoot, dip and rebound of one zone's heating calls. Add one per zone.

user.title: Furnace energy
user.description: A modelled energy meter (kWh) for the energy dashboard, from the furnace state and a power for each state. Add one for the blower (kW, learned from a power sensor or typed) and one for the gas (the furnace input in BTU/h).

data.name: Name
data.power_entity: Whole-house power sensor (to learn the blower)
data.learn_days: Days of history to learn from (2-60)
data.blower_curve: Blower curve (flow = static, from the data sheet)

data_description.climate_entities: Every zone's thermostat; the furnace state is read from all of them.
data_description.power_entity: Optional. Steps in this sensor when the furnace changes state set the fan and heating powers (needs several days; every 6 hours it refreshes). The powers typed below are used until then, and for any state it cannot learn.
data_description.power_unit: kW, or BTU/h for gas input (80,000 BTU/h is 23.4 kW). Stored in kW.
data_description.fan: Leave a state blank for zero.
data_description.cool_tons: Air conditioner size in tons (12,000 BTU/h each), as 'tonnes' are used in Canada. It sets the cooling power and overrides the box above. A ton is heat moved, not electricity; for the electric meter type the kW drawn instead.
data_description.afue: Gas furnaces: the AFUE from the nameplate, such as 95. Leave empty for electric.
data_description.blower_curve: Airflow = external static, from the blower's data sheet, such as '400 cfm = 0.30 inWC, 800 = 0.20, 1200 = 0.05'. Units go on the first point and carry to the rest (CFM and inches of water column unless you say otherwise: l/s, m3/s, Pa).
data_description.ac_sensible_btuh: The sensible (not total) cooling capacity at the rating point, from the data sheet, in BTU/h. Leave empty if unknown.
data_description.area_id: Which room the furnace (its air handler) sits in. The Loads tab shows it beside the equipment.

user.title: Shadow zone (with sun)
user.description: Says whether a heating call starting now could be skipped, counting the sun on this room's windows and roofs (hypothesis 17), and forecasts the room for the next day with a simulated thermostat (hypothesis 16). Nothing is switched. With a and c left empty, the model is learned from the recorder and refreshed every 6 hours; the shadow sensor's attributes show what it learned and how well it forecasts. Each zone also gets a Forecast and a Target sensor, and appears in the Thermal Lab panel.

data.name: Name
data.roofs: Roofs with windows in this room
data.h: Heating rate h (degrees per hour of call), optional
data.target_swing: Target wave: swing (degrees either side of the mean)
data.target_band: Target wave: comfort band (degrees either side)

data_description.room_entity: Used instead of the thermostat's own reading when set.
data_description.a: Leave both empty to learn them from the last 14 days of history (a few days of data are needed first).
data_description.c: Leave both empty to learn them from the last 14 days of history (a few days of data are needed first).
data_description.tolerance: How far below the setpoint the room may drift.
data_description.max_dip: Skip a heating call only if the room stays within this of the setpoint.
data_description.windows: Faces that have windows letting the sun in (the glass term).
data_description.roofs: Tick the house's roofs (set on the integration) that have windows or skylights in this room.
data_description.shade_below: Leave empty to use the house value.
data_description.g: Only used with a and c.
data_description.sunlit_walls: Faces of solid wall the sun hits. Learned separately from the windows: sun on a wall warms it slowly.
data_description.below_ground: Tick for a room whose walls are in the soil. The model then also learns how fast the room trades heat with the ground.
data_description.ground_entity: Optional soil or ground temperature. Leave empty to use the annual ground wave set on the integration.
data_description.h: How fast the room warms while the furnace runs for this zone. Leave empty to learn it from the calls in the recorder.
data_description.deadband: How far below the setpoint a call starts, in the forecast's simulated thermostat (default 0.1; measured calls start a median 0.05 to 0.07 below).
data_description.target_mean: Leave empty to target the thermostat's setpoint instead of a daily wave.
data_description.target_peak_hour: Default 15 (3 pm): the outdoor wave peaks 1 to 3 hours after solar noon (hypothesis 02).
data_description.neighbours: Zones whose temperature and heating calls warm this one, for its learned model and forecast. Leave empty: the zone that heats most is every other zone's neighbour, and all the others are its.
data_description.area_id: With House Structure set up, the room's windows, roofs, sunlit walls, thermostat (from its register), room sensor and below-ground setting come from there, and the window, roof and wall fields below are ignored. A thermostat or room sensor picked below wins.
data_description.climate_entity: Needed unless the room (area) has a register in House Structure.

user.title: Detached building
user.description: A building with no duct or heating connection to the house, such as a garage. Its rooms are taken out of the house's Manual J and sized on their own in the Loads tab. Give it the House Structure parts of its rooms (walls, roof, windows) and pick its Home Assistant areas here.

data_description.areas: The Home Assistant areas that make up the building. A room is only sized if House Structure has parts in its area.
data_description.indoor_heat_c: Leave empty to use the house's design indoor temperature.
data_description.indoor_cool_c: Leave empty to use the house's design indoor temperature.
